newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end down 2.4 pct after hitting 1997 low.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end down 2.4 pct after hitting 1997 low.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares ended sharply lower on Monday, bouncing slightly off a new 1997 low, after being pulled down by worries over the central bank's new foreign exchange restrictions.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 24.07 points, or 2.40 percent, down at 978.56. It earlier hit a low of 976.26, its lowest level in 1997.
Analysts said central Bank Negara Malaysia's move to restrict foreign exchange offer-side swap transactions to $2 million contributed to the market's bearishness.
"It doesn't help stocks when one imposes capital market restrictions," said Jonathan Duckett, an analyst at Mohaiyani Securities.

Telekom fell 45 cents to 9.25 ringgit, a new 1997 low. The company on Friday announced a 5.7 percent growth in earnings for the six months to June 30, 1997, falling short of most analysts' expectations.
Telekom has a 10 percent weighting on the index.
Rumours of a large monthly trade deficit for June added to the market's bearishness, analysts said.
"It's insane for anyone to take a position in the market at this time," said Duckett, pointing to continuing currency instability.
Dealers said they saw foreign selling of blue-chips.

"There were genuine sellers in the morning, but the short-sellers came in in the afternoon," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage. He noted that many of the blue-chips like Telekom, Tenaga and Maybank, were sold down on heavy volume.
Tenaga fell 30 cents to 10.10 ringgit while Maybank shed 50 cents to 24.40.

"I certainly believe it was the foreigners who were selling. It would not be worth it for the local institutions to start selling at this level," said Ramlan Ahmad, senior manager at fund managers Commerce MGI in Kuala Lumpur.
The outlook remained bleak for share prices, said analysts.
"The selling is no longer about corporate fundamentals," said Ramlan. "They are talking about currency instability and the like".
"It is going to take at least a month to stabilise," said Duckett.
At the close, market volume stood at 209 million shares, valued at 1.4 billion ringgit. Losers swamped gainers 621 to 52.
